WhatsApp.desc: Primary first-class channel across ALL products. Meta Cloud API integration. Receives inbound messages (text, interactive button replies, voice notes as audio URLs) via HTTPS webhook. Sends outbound via META Graph API /messages endpoint.

deploy.note: Requires approved WhatsApp Business Account (WABA), a registered phone number, and an HTTPS webhook endpoint with TLS.

WhatsApp.notes: Meta sends ALL user messages via POST to your registered /webhook endpoint. You must respond HTTP 200 within 5s or Meta retries. Voice notes arrive as audio URLs — Channel Gateway downloads the file, passes to Whisper STT, then sends text to LangGraph.

Whisper STT.desc: OpenAI Whisper speech-to-text, used to convert WhatsApp voice notes into text before passing to LangGraph. Turkish language support. Can run CPU-only (slower) or GPU (faster-whisper).

deploy.install: pip install openai-whisper OR pip install faster-whisper
deploy.note: Runs as a sidecar or inline function in the Channel Gateway service. GPU node preferred for <2s latency.

config.n: base / medium / large based on GPU

Whisper STT.notes: faster-whisper (CTranslate2 backend) is 4-8x faster than standard Whisper. For GU v1, medium model gives best TR accuracy. Audio file is fetched from Meta CDN, transcribed in-memory, text returned to Channel Gateway.

sample.code:
curl -X POST http://whisper:9000/transcribe   -F "audio=@voice-note.ogg"   -F "language=tr"   -F "model=large-v3"
# → {"text":"merhaba nasılsınız","language":"tr","duration_s":3.5}

errors.symptom: Transcription returns empty text for valid audio
errors.action: Audio format mismatch — Whisper expects 16kHz mono. Channel gateway must resample WhatsApp OGG (48kHz stereo) before forwarding. Check `model_load_seconds` metric for cold-start delay.

errors.symptom: GPU OOM on long voice notes (>2min)
errors.action: Whisper batches audio chunks; reduce `max_chunk_seconds` in deployment config from default 30 to 20. Or scale to a larger GPU.

Embed widget.desc: Lightweight JavaScript widget (< 20KB) that manufacturers embed in their websites. Opens a chat UI that calls the ARDICTECH API. Configurable branding, theme, initial questions. Handles streaming responses.

deploy.note: Build with Vite. Serve from MinIO or CDN. No iframe required.

Embed widget.notes: The widget sends messages via REST to Kong → FastAPI → LangGraph. Supports streaming (Server-Sent Events). Auth is via an ephemeral session token issued on widget initialization.

ops.log: Browser console + server-side RUM in Grafana Faro
ops.trace: Widget emits widget.session_start → propagated as X-Trace-Id

sample.code:
<!-- Drop into the host page -->
<script src="https://cdn.ardictech.com/widget/v1/widget.js" defer></script>
<script>
  window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
    ARDICWidget.init({
      tenant: 'kale-seramik',
      apiUrl: 'https://api.kale.ardictech.com',
      locale: 'tr',
      position: 'bottom-right'
    });
  });
</script>

errors.symptom: Widget does not render after page load
errors.action: CSP blocking — host page must allow `connect-src` to API URL and `script-src` to CDN. Check browser console for CSP violation reports.

errors.symptom: Session lost on page refresh
errors.action: Widget uses sessionStorage by default; for cross-page persistence, configure with `storage:"local"`. Tenant admin can toggle in dashboard.

Outlook / Graph.desc: Microsoft Graph API subscription that fires a webhook notification when a new email arrives in the Türk Re insurance mailbox. The platform processes the email content (subject, body, attachments) as a trigger for the insurance triage workflow.

deploy.note: Requires Azure App Registration with Mail.Read permission. Subscription expires every 3 days and must be renewed.

Outlook / Graph.notes: Graph webhooks send a validation request first (must echo validationToken). Change notifications arrive as JSON with message ID. Platform then fetches full message via GET /messages/{id} with attachments.

Web chat.desc: Browser-based chat interface for internal teams and demos. OpenWebUI (or Chainlit) connects to FastAPI backend. Supports streaming, file upload, conversation history, and admin mode.

deploy.note: Configured to point at our FastAPI/LangGraph backend, not directly at Ollama.

Web chat.notes: OpenWebUI is used for internal access and demos. It is NOT the customer-facing product. The embedded widget is the customer channel for Web Asistan. Web Chat integrates with Keycloak for SSO.

ops.metrics: Vercel/Cloudflare edge metrics + browser RUM (Grafana Faro)
ops.log: Edge logs + frontend errors → Grafana Faro
ops.trace: SSR pages emit webchat.page.{route}; WS sessions emit webchat.session.{id}

errors.symptom: WebSocket disconnects every 60s
errors.action: Kong default idle timeout is 60s. Set `upstream_read_timeout: 3600` for the `/ws/*` route, OR enable WS ping/pong with 30s interval from the client.

errors.symptom: Streaming responses arrive all at once instead of incrementally
errors.action: Check that the response goes through Kong with `request_buffering: false`. Buffering is enabled by default and breaks SSE/streaming.

Teams bot.desc: Microsoft Teams channel for CWF manufacturing intelligence. Receives manufacturing queries from factory teams via Teams chat, routes to Channel Gateway, and streams responses back. Adaptive Cards for rich output.

deploy.note: Register in Azure Bot Service. Requires public HTTPS endpoint for Bot Framework messaging endpoint.

Teams bot.notes: The Teams bot is implemented as a FastAPI application using Bot Framework SDK. Messages are normalized to the Channel Gateway format and processed identically to other channels.

sample.code:
# Simulate a Teams message webhook from Bot Framework
curl -X POST http://teams-bot:3978/api/messages   -H "Authorization: Bearer $BF_TOKEN"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"type":"message","from":{"id":"user1"},"text":"OEE status line 3?","conversation":{"id":"c1"}}'

errors.symptom: Bot does not respond but logs show 200 OK
errors.action: Bot Framework requires reply within 15s; if LangGraph takes longer, send a typing indicator via `turnContext.sendActivities` and stream the final answer. Check Adaptive Card schema if rich response fails.

errors.symptom: Authentication errors on first message after deploy
errors.action: BF_TOKEN env var must match the Microsoft App registration. Rotate via Vault path `apps/teams-bot/bf-token` and restart pod.

Min. dashboard.desc: Minimal administrative dashboard for tenant management, billing oversight, audit log review, and platform health. Built with Next.js or simple server-rendered UI. NOT the customer-facing product.

deploy.note: Deployed as a K8s deployment behind Kong with admin-only JWT auth.

Min. dashboard.notes: Serves as the operations control panel. Shows per-tenant usage, billing invoices (iyzico/Stripe), active sessions, audit log search, and ArgoCD deployment status.

sample.code:
# Admin API: list tenants
curl -X GET https://admin.kale.ardictech.com/api/tenants   -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_JWT"
# → [{"id":"kale-seramik","plan":"enterprise","active":true},...]

errors.symptom: Tenant list shows stale data
errors.action: Dashboard uses ISR with 60s revalidate. Force refresh via `?refresh=true` query param, or hit the admin API directly (`/api/tenants`).

errors.symptom: Login redirects to Keycloak but bounces back to login
errors.action: Redirect URI mismatch — Keycloak client config must include `https://admin.{tenant}.ardictech.com/api/auth/callback/keycloak` exactly. Wildcards not supported.

Channel gateway.desc: Central normalization and routing service. Receives messages from all channels (WhatsApp, Widget, Outlook, Teams, Web Chat), normalizes them to a standard MessageEnvelope format, and dispatches to LangGraph. One brain, many mouths.

deploy.note: Exposes channel-specific webhook endpoints. Stateless: session context loaded from Redis.

Channel gateway.notes: This is the single entry point for ALL user interactions. It enforces tenant isolation at the boundary, rate-limits per channel, and adds metadata (tenant, channel, session) to every message envelope before routing.

ops.trace: Langfuse: channel.{name}.inbound (one trace per inbound message)

sample.code:
# Receive a WhatsApp webhook (simulated)
curl -X POST http://channel-gateway:8000/webhook/whatsapp   -H "X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<meta-hmac>"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"entry":[{"changes":[{"value":{"messages":[{"from":"+90...","text":{"body":"merhaba"}}]}}]}]}'

errors.symptom: Webhook returns 502 to Meta
errors.action: Check LangGraph readiness (`kubectl get pod langgraph`). Gateway is a thin proxy — issue is almost always upstream. Verify Redis connectivity too (`redis-cli -h redis ping`).

errors.symptom: WhatsApp messages duplicated in logs
errors.action: Meta retries on 5xx. Confirm the gateway returns 200 within 5s even when LangGraph is slow — enqueue to Redis and ack immediately if needed.

Kong.desc: API gateway handling all inbound traffic. Manages rate limiting, JWT authentication validation, CORS, request logging, and routing to upstream FastAPI services. Configured declaratively via kong.yaml.

deploy.note: Runs in DB-less mode with declarative config. Two ports: 8000 (proxy) and 8001 (admin API, internal only).

Kong.notes: Kong OPA plugin calls the OPA service for every request with policy data extracted from the JWT. This enforces multi-tenant isolation at the gateway level before any request reaches FastAPI.

ops.log: {service="kong"} | json | level="error"  (access logs on a separate channel)

sample.code:
# Add a new route forwarding to FastAPI service
curl -X POST http://kong:8001/services/fastapi/routes   -d "name=chat"   -d "paths[]=/api/chat"   -d "strip_path=true"

errors.symptom: Random 502s on `/api/*` routes
errors.action: Kong upstream health check declared FastAPI unhealthy. Inspect `/upstreams/fastapi/health` — usually a transient FastAPI pod restart. Increase `healthy.successes` from default 1 to 3 to be more forgiving.

errors.symptom: Plugin not applying to a route
errors.action: Plugin order matters — `key-auth` must come before `rate-limiting`. List plugins on the route: `GET /routes/{route_id}/plugins` and reorder via `before`/`after`.

FastAPI.desc: Core application server. Handles all business logic, exposes REST endpoints for channel callbacks and admin operations, WebSocket endpoints for streaming responses, and serves as the orchestration coordinator between all services.

deploy.install: pip install fastapi uvicorn[standard] sqlalchemy asyncpg
deploy.note: Runs as K8s deployment with HPA. Multiple replicas behind Kong.

FastAPI.notes: Each product (WA, GU, CWF, Insurance) is a FastAPI "router" mounted under a common application. This keeps code modular while sharing middleware (auth, logging, rate-limit) across all products.

errors.symptom: 5xx spikes during high traffic
errors.action: asyncpg pool exhaustion — check `pg_stat_activity` for connection count. Raise pool size (default 20) only if PostgreSQL can handle it (`max_connections` in PG config).

errors.symptom: JWT validation fails with "Invalid signature" randomly
errors.action: Keycloak JWKS cache stale after key rotation. Set cache TTL to <=5min in FastAPI middleware. Manual purge: restart pod or POST `/admin/cache/purge`.

Keycloak.desc: Identity and access management. Issues JWT access tokens, manages realms per tenant, handles social login, and federates with Microsoft Entra ID for enterprise customers. Single source of auth truth.

deploy.note: Requires PostgreSQL backend. Configure realm export for GitOps. Port 8080.

Keycloak.notes: Each tenant gets its own Keycloak realm provisioned automatically via Tenant Provisioning service. Realm-level isolation ensures no cross-tenant token acceptance.

sample.code:
# Get an admin token, then list realms
TOKEN=$(curl -s -d "client_id=admin-cli" -d "username=admin"   -d "password=$ADMIN_PASS" -d "grant_type=password"   http://keycloak:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token   | jq -r .access_token)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://keycloak:8080/admin/realms

errors.symptom: Login slow (>5s) under load
errors.action: Realm key cache cold or DB contention. Inspect `pg_stat_activity` for Keycloak queries. Pre-warm by hitting `/realms/{realm}/.well-known/openid-configuration` after each pod start.

errors.symptom: Tokens issued but refresh fails
errors.action: Refresh token TTL exceeded (default 30min). Either extend TTL in realm settings, OR ensure clients refresh proactively at 80% of access token TTL.

Entra federation.desc: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) federation with Keycloak. Enterprise customers log in with their Microsoft credentials. Keycloak acts as a broker, mapping Entra claims to platform roles. ⚠ v5.1 SPLIT: basic per-instance Keycloak ↔ customer AD/Entra OIDC federation ships in INSURANCE D8 (day-one runtime dependency of the on-prem instance). This FIN component covers only enterprise-wide hardening + multi-customer federation rollout for Astra.

deploy.image: No container — Entra is external. Config in Keycloak.
deploy.install: Configure Identity Provider in Keycloak admin
deploy.note: Register ARDICTECH as an app in customer Azure tenant. Configure OIDC federation in Keycloak.

Entra federation.notes: Required for Astra enterprise use cases where customers are Microsoft-first. Keycloak handles the OIDC broker pattern transparently — users do not see two login screens.

OPA.desc: Open Policy Agent. Enforces fine-grained authorization policies written in Rego. Evaluates every API request: tenant isolation, role-based access, feature flags per product tier. Kong calls OPA before forwarding requests.

deploy.note: Bundle mode: policies loaded from Git repo or bundle server. Port 8181.

OPA.notes: Rego policies check: (1) JWT tenant claim matches URL path tenant, (2) JWT role has permission for requested action, (3) product feature is enabled for this tenant tier. Decisions are cached per JWT for 30s.

ops.log: {service="opa"} | json  (decision logs on a separate sink → Loki tenant)

errors.symptom: Policy evaluations slow (>50ms)
errors.action: Decision log shipping is synchronous by default. Set `decision_logs.console: false` and use the bundle plugin for async shipping. Inspect policy complexity — nested iteration is O(n^2).

errors.symptom: Bundle fails to load on pod start
errors.action: Bundle URL (Vault, OCI, HTTPS) unreachable. Check `/v1/status` for bundle status. Fallback: bake the policy into the image as `/policies/` for emergency.

Tenant provisioning.desc: Automated tenant onboarding service. A single POST /provision call creates a Kubernetes namespace, PostgreSQL schema, Keycloak realm, Kong routes, and Qdrant collection — all wired together. Zero manual steps.

deploy.install: Embedded in FastAPI as a router
deploy.note: Must run with K8s ServiceAccount that has cluster-admin or namespace-create privileges.

Tenant provisioning.notes: Idempotent: calling /provision with the same tenant ID twice is safe. Tenant namespaces enforce resource quotas (CPU/memory) and network policies (no cross-namespace traffic).

ops.trace: tenant.provision.{step}  (steps: realm · db · qdrant · k8s · opa)

errors.symptom: Provisioning job stuck at "qdrant" step
errors.action: Qdrant cluster may be over-replica-limit. Inspect Qdrant pod count and `/cluster` endpoint. Service retries with backoff — kill the job manually if Qdrant needs scaling first.

errors.symptom: Tenant created but admin cannot log in
errors.action: Realm created but client credentials not pushed. Check `provision.steps.realm` audit table. Re-run just the credential step: POST `/provision/{tenant}/repair?step=keycloak_client`.

LangGraph.desc: The single multi-agent orchestration framework for ALL products. Each product defines a LangGraph StateGraph with nodes (RAG, tool-call, classify, decide, respond). Shared graph patterns: intent routing, tool calling, hybrid decision, response formatting.

deploy.note: No official Docker image. Package as custom FastAPI service. GPU not required for orchestration. Port 8001.

LangGraph.notes: KEY DESIGN: LangGraph is stateful. Each session has a unique thread_id. State is checkpointed to PostgreSQL (for durability) and Redis (for fast access). LLM ranks/extracts; the Hybrid Decision Engine decides. Never the reverse.

ops.trace: langgraph.{agent}.{node}  (every node + every LLM call recorded in Langfuse)

errors.symptom: Agent runs but final output is empty
errors.action: Guardrails validation failure caught silently. Check Langfuse trace for `guardrails.{rail}.validate` span with `result:fail`. Rail spec mismatch with model output schema — update rail YAML.

errors.symptom: Workflow stuck after first node
errors.action: PostgresSaver checkpoint failure — check `pg_stat_activity` for blocked LangGraph queries. Likely WAL bloat or replication lag. Truncate checkpoint table or restart LangGraph pod.

errors.symptom: Same query returns different answers each run
errors.action: Temperature too high OR retrieval non-deterministic. Set `temperature: 0` for deterministic queries (analytics) and verify Qdrant search uses `consistency: strong`.

Hybrid decision engine.desc: A Python module embedded within LangGraph (no separate service). The LLM extracts and ranks candidates; this engine applies deterministic rules to make the final decision and writes every decision to the PostgreSQL audit log with full reasoning trace.

deploy.image: Embedded Python module in LangGraph service
deploy.note: Rules defined as YAML files in Git. Hot-reloaded on config change. The same engine serves Insurance (Yeni/Yenileme/Geçmişte), GU audit, and CWF classification.

config.n: Minimum LLM confidence to pass to rules

Hybrid decision engine.notes: This is the architectural spine of the platform. Audit trail requirement: every decision record includes: input, LLM output, rule applied, final decision, timestamp, user_id, tenant_id. Required for IATF 16949, AS9100, KVKK compliance.

ops.health: In-process module within LangGraph; health reported via parent service

errors.symptom: Decision always falls through to default rule
errors.action: Rules YAML not loaded — hot reload may have missed the file change. `kubectl logs langgraph | grep "rules loaded"` should show N rules. If 0, fix YAML syntax (most likely indentation).

errors.symptom: Audit log missing for some decisions
errors.action: Async insert may have failed under load. Engine uses fire-and-forget by default. Check `pg_stat_activity` for `INSERT INTO decisions` blocked queries. Switch to sync insert for compliance-critical flows.

n8n.desc: Low-code workflow automation for manufacturing operations. Triggers automated alerts, escalations, and reports. Connects to Teams, email, ARMES, and various manufacturing systems without custom code. Used by CWF for n8n-as-ops-automation.

deploy.note: Configure with PostgreSQL persistence (not default SQLite for production). Port 5678.

n8n.notes: n8n workflows are triggered by LangGraph via REST webhook POST. Manufacturing-specific flows: OEE alert → Teams notification, maintenance ticket → ARMES, daily summary → WhatsApp.

sample.code:
# Trigger an OEE-alert webhook workflow
curl -X POST http://n8n:5678/webhook/oee-alert   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"line":"3","oee":0.62,"threshold":0.75}'

errors.symptom: Webhook trigger fires twice for one event
errors.action: n8n retries on workflow error. Ensure your workflow is idempotent OR enable "execute once" setting in the workflow settings.

errors.symptom: Workflow times out at 30s but should run longer
errors.action: Default timeout. Set `WORKFLOWS_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=300` or per-workflow via the settings panel. For >5min workflows, use Temporal instead.

Temporal.desc: Durable workflow execution engine for long-running processes that must survive service restarts, network failures, or indefinite waits. Required for Astra use cases with multi-day SLA-bound workflows (insurance processing, procurement approvals). ⚠ v5.1 GATED (task G7, 80h): build ONLY if a confirmed Astra UC requires durable multi-day HITL workflows that LangGraph Postgres checkpointing cannot cover. Default = NOT built.

deploy.note: Requires PostgreSQL for persistence. Port 7233 (gRPC). Web UI on 8080.

Temporal.notes: LangGraph workflows that may take minutes-to-hours (e.g. waiting for a human approval step, polling an external API for status) are wrapped in Temporal Activities. This gives automatic retry, timeout, and audit trail.

sample.code:
from temporalio.client import Client
client = await Client.connect("temporal:7233")
handle = await client.start_workflow(
    InsuranceTriageWorkflow.run,
    args=["case-12345"],
    id=f"insurance-{case_id}",
    task_queue="insurance"
)
await handle.result()  # awaits completion (may take minutes-to-hours)

errors.symptom: Workflows complete but `await result()` hangs
errors.action: Client is waiting for a return value the workflow never set. Check Temporal UI for workflow status — if it shows COMPLETED but no result, the workflow returned None. Add return value to workflow function.

errors.symptom: High Postgres CPU correlated with Temporal
errors.action: Persistence cleanup not running — Temporal stores history forever by default. Configure `retention: 30d` per namespace, and verify cleanup workflow is running.

vLLM.desc: High-throughput LLM inference server for Llama-3-8B (and optionally 70B). OpenAI-compatible API. Runs on sovereign GPU nodes on Netaş/OSB Cloud. PagedAttention enables high concurrency with low memory.

deploy.note: Requires NVIDIA GPU K8s node. Set --tensor-parallel-size for multi-GPU. Port 8000.

vLLM.notes: vLLM is NOT called directly by LangGraph. All LLM calls go through LiteLLM proxy, which routes to vLLM. This enables seamless model switching, fallback to Ollama for dev, and future cloud model opt-in without changing agent code.

ops.health: GET http://vllm:8000/health → 200 (returns healthy when model loaded)

sample.code:
# vLLM is OpenAI-compatible; in production it's called through LiteLLM
curl -X POST http://vllm:8000/v1/chat/completions   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"model":"meta-llama/Llama-3-8B-Instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'

errors.symptom: First request after deploy takes 60+ seconds
errors.action: Model loading on cold start. Pre-warm in pod readiness check — wait for `/health` to return 200 before adding pod to LB. Increase pod start grace period to 90s in K8s deployment.

errors.symptom: OOM crash under heavy concurrent load
errors.action: `gpu_memory_utilization` too aggressive. Reduce from 0.90 to 0.85, OR lower `max_model_len` (default 8192). Check vLLM logs for "CUDA out of memory".

LiteLLM.desc: Unified LLM proxy that translates ALL LangGraph requests to the appropriate backend (vLLM, Ollama, Azure OpenAI). Single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Handles retries, fallback routing, cost tracking, and usage metrics.

deploy.note: Configure litellm_config.yaml with model list. Port 4000. Expose only internally, never publicly.

LiteLLM.notes: litellm_config.yaml defines: model_list with each provider, fallbacks array, max_retries. This is where "gated off sovereign" is enforced: Azure OpenAI is in the config but its cost_map flag disables it unless explicitly enabled per tenant.

sample.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://litellm:4000", api_key=os.getenv("LITELLM_KEY"))
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sonnet-4.6",  # LiteLLM routes to Anthropic
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"OEE forecast for line 3?"}]
)
# All LangGraph LLM calls flow through this client, never direct to providers

errors.symptom: Fallback to Ollama in production
errors.action: Primary provider (vLLM/Anthropic) failed. Check `litellm_fallback_total` metric. Common cause: rate limit hit. Adjust per-key rate limits in `litellm_config.yaml`.

errors.symptom: Cost tracking shows zero usage
errors.action: Langfuse callback not configured. Set `LANGFUSE_HOST` env var. Check LiteLLM logs for "callback init" errors.

Ollama.desc: Lightweight local LLM runner for development and low-latency lightweight tasks. Supports Llama 3, Mistral, Phi-3. No GPU required (uses CPU with quantization). Used in dev environments and for non-critical lightweight generations.

deploy.note: Port 11434. Model weights downloaded on first pull. Mount persistent volume for models.

Ollama.notes: In production, vLLM is primary. Ollama is secondary/fallback in LiteLLM config. In development, Ollama serves as the sole LLM to avoid GPU requirement.

ops.metrics: Not native; expose via ollama-exporter sidecar if needed
ops.trace: Dev / test only; not part of production trace topology

sample.code: curl -X POST http://ollama:11434/api/chat   -d '{"model":"llama3:8b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":false}'

errors.symptom: "Model not found" error
errors.action: Pull the model first: `ollama pull llama3:8b`. Persistent volume mounted at `/data/models` — check disk space.

errors.symptom: Responses slow in dev environment
errors.action: Ollama on CPU is slow for >7B models. Use Q4 quantization (`llama3:8b-q4_K_M`) or accept ~30s response times in dev.

MLflow.desc: ML experiment tracking and model registry. Tracks LLM evaluation runs (RAGAS scores), prompt versions, fine-tuning experiments. All production model versions must be registered here before deployment.

deploy.note: Server mode: mlflow server --backend-store-uri postgresql:// --default-artifact-root s3://mlflow/ . Port 5000.

MLflow.notes: All RAGAS evaluation results (faithfulness, relevance, groundedness) are logged to MLflow. This creates a traceable history of model quality over time and enables A/B comparison of prompt changes.

ops.metrics: Not native; instrument client-side or use mlflow-prometheus-exporter
ops.trace: experiment-id and run-id are the trace keys; correlate via mlflow.{exp_id}.{run_id}

sample.code:
import mlflow
mlflow.set_tracking_uri("http://mlflow:5000")
with mlflow.start_run(run_name="ragas-eval-2026-06"):
    mlflow.log_metric("faithfulness", 0.87)
    mlflow.log_metric("answer_relevance", 0.91)
    mlflow.log_artifact("eval_results.json")

errors.symptom: Artifacts not appearing in MinIO
errors.action: MinIO credentials wrong or bucket missing. Verify `mlflow-artifacts/` bucket exists. Check MLflow logs for "NoSuchBucket" errors.

errors.symptom: Run names duplicated
errors.action: MLflow generates random names on duplicate `run_name`. Set `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` per-experiment and use `start_run(run_name=)` consistently.

Prompt store.desc: PostgreSQL-backed prompt template registry. Stores versioned, language-parameterized prompt templates for each agent type (RAG, classification, extraction, summary). LangGraph fetches active prompts at runtime.

deploy.install: PostgreSQL table: prompts(id, name, version, language, template, active)
deploy.note: No separate container. CRUD endpoints in FastAPI admin router. Templates support Jinja2 variables.

Prompt store.notes: Prompts are versioned. Rollback is a single SQL UPDATE. Turkish and English variants of each prompt are stored separately. Guardrails AI rail specs are also versioned here.

errors.symptom: Wrong language template returned
errors.action: Cache key includes lang, but client passed wrong header. Verify `?lang=tr` query param OR `Accept-Language: tr` header. Fallback always goes to EN if TR missing.

errors.symptom: Version "latest" returns old template
errors.action: Active version not updated. Check `prompts.versions` table — must mark new version `active=true` and old `active=false` in one tx. Use POST `/admin/prompts/{id}/promote/{version}`.

Langfuse.desc: LLM observability platform. Every LangGraph execution generates a Langfuse trace with all LLM calls, latencies, token counts, retrieved chunks, and final outputs. Essential for debugging, cost analysis, and quality audit.

deploy.note: Requires PostgreSQL. Configure S3 (MinIO) for media. Port 3000. Auth via Keycloak OIDC.

Langfuse.notes: LangGraph integrates via LangfuseCallbackHandler (SDK, in-process). LiteLLM sends usage callbacks. Combined, every production LLM call has: trace_id, session_id, tenant_id, prompt_name, model, latency, tokens, cost estimate.

ops.metrics: Ingestion-rate via internal metrics endpoint; UI shows live trace counts
ops.trace: Langfuse IS the trace store. Query via UI (http://langfuse:3000) or SDK

sample.code:
from langfuse import Langfuse
lf = Langfuse(host="http://langfuse:3000")
trace = lf.trace(name="galip_oee_query", user_id="op-123", tenant_id="kale")
trace.span(name="rag.retrieve", input={"q":"OEE line 3"}).end(output=[...])
trace.span(name="llm.generate", model="sonnet-4.6").end(output="...")

errors.symptom: Traces appear in UI but no spans visible
errors.action: Callback fired but spans not flushed. Add `langfuse.flush()` before exit or use context manager. Async batching has a 10s delay by default.

errors.symptom: Cost shows $0 for all traces
errors.action: Model name in trace does not match Langfuse model catalog. Add custom model pricing via `langfuse.create_model(...)` for non-standard names like `sonnet-4.6`.

Guardrails AI.desc: Validates LLM inputs and outputs against defined Rail specs. Ensures structured output format (JSON schema), detects and blocks toxic content, validates extracted fields (VKN format, date ranges, Faaliyet codes) before downstream use.

deploy.note: No separate service. Instantiated as GuardedLLM wrapper around LiteLLM in LangGraph nodes. Rail specs stored in Prompt Store.

config.n: YAML rail spec per agent type

Guardrails AI.notes: Insurance-specific rails: VKN 10-digit validation, date format, Faaliyet sektör code in approved list. GU-specific rails: OEE value in [0,1], equipment ID matches known asset list. Cross-product: no PII in LLM output.

ops.health: In-process within LangGraph; no separate endpoint

sample.code:
from guardrails import Guard
guard = Guard.from_rail("rails/quality_metric_response.rail")
validated = guard.parse(llm_output)
# Raises ValidationError if rail violated; LangGraph handles retry

errors.symptom: Validation always passes even when output is bad
errors.action: Rail file not loaded — check path. Default Guard auto-loads from current working directory. Set `RAILS_DIR=/app/rails` and verify `Guard.from_rail("quality.rail")` succeeds at startup.

errors.symptom: ValidationError raised but LangGraph does not retry
errors.action: LangGraph node must catch ValidationError and re-invoke LLM with feedback. Check the node code — generic `except Exception` may swallow it without retry logic.

LlamaIndex.desc: Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework. Handles document ingestion (chunking, embedding, indexing), query engines, and retrieval pipelines. All product RAG flows (catalog, ARMES docs, insurance submissions) go through LlamaIndex.

deploy.image: Embedded Python library in LangGraph service
deploy.note: No separate service. Runs in LangGraph agent process. Requires Qdrant and/or pgvector.

LlamaIndex.notes: BAAI/bge-m3 embedding model supports Turkish (critical for GU and CWF). Chunks are stored in Qdrant with metadata (tenant_id, source, doc_type). Retrieval always filters by tenant_id to prevent cross-tenant leakage.

sample.code:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex
from llama_index.vector_stores.qdrant import QdrantVectorStore
qstore = QdrantVectorStore(client=qc, collection_name="kale_catalog")
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_vector_store(qstore)
results = index.as_retriever(similarity_top_k=5).retrieve(
    "OEE thresholds for Kale plant line 3"
)

errors.symptom: Retrieval returns 0 results for valid queries
errors.action: Collection empty or wrong embedding model. Verify `qc.count(collection_name)` >0. Mismatch between indexing-time and query-time embeddings will return near-random results.

errors.symptom: Retrieval slow (>500ms)
errors.action: Top-K too high or HNSW config off. Reduce `similarity_top_k` to 5. Tune Qdrant HNSW (`ef_construct: 200, m: 16`) at collection creation time — cannot change later.

Qdrant / pgvector.desc: Dual-mode vector search: Qdrant for semantic similarity (dense vectors, 768-dim), pgvector for filtered SQL-native vector queries. Qdrant is the primary vector store; pgvector handles cases where vector search co-queries relational data.

deploy.note: Port 6333 (HTTP), 6334 (gRPC). Enable snapshots for backup. pgvector: CREATE EXTENSION vector; in PostgreSQL.

config.n: Store vectors on disk for large collections

Qdrant / pgvector.notes: Collections are tenant-namespaced: {tenant_id}_{collection_type}. This gives hardware-level tenant isolation for vector data. pgvector is used when the query needs BOTH semantic similarity AND relational filtering (e.g., filter by date range AND semantic similarity).

ops.health: See Qdrant (L6) for the deployed service; this entry is the SDK + embedding pattern
ops.metrics: Collection-level metrics via Qdrant admin API

sample.code:
from qdrant_client import QdrantClient
qc = QdrantClient(url="http://qdrant:6333")
qc.upsert(
    collection_name="kale_catalog",
    points=[{"id":1,"vector":[0.1]*1024,"payload":{"sku":"K-001","name":"Tile A"}}]
)

errors.symptom: Upsert silently succeeds but search returns nothing
errors.action: Vector dimension mismatch — Qdrant accepts the upsert but search filters it. Verify embedding dimension matches collection schema (e.g., 1024 for bge-m3).

errors.symptom: Tenant data leaking into wrong collection
errors.action: Collection name not tenant-scoped. Must use `{tenant}_{purpose}` format (e.g., `kale_catalog`). Audit via `qc.get_collections()` — refactor any non-scoped collection.

Memori.desc: Dual-layer memory system for LangGraph. Session memory: active conversation context stored in Redis (TTL=4h). Profile memory: long-term user preferences, interaction history, and learned patterns stored in PostgreSQL. Serves query classes 3 (contextual) and shallow-4 (profile-aware).

deploy.note: Expose as internal REST service. Session data auto-expires from Redis. Profile data partitioned by tenant_id in PostgreSQL.

Memori.notes: Memory injection into LangGraph: system prompt includes last N turns (session) + top-3 relevant profile facts (profile). This avoids context-window explosion while maintaining coherent multi-turn behavior.

errors.symptom: Session memory empty even after multiple turns
errors.action: Memori only persists once per turn. Check that LangGraph calls `memori.write(session_id, turn)` after each completion. Race condition possible if multiple instances; use Redis lock if needed.

errors.symptom: Profile memory bleeds across tenants
errors.action: Profile keyed by `user_id` only — must be `{tenant}:{user_id}`. Migration: rewrite all profile keys with tenant prefix; old ones unreachable.

LightRAG.desc: Knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval for class-5 document queries over ARMES docs, SOPs, and manuals. Builds a graph of entities and relations from documents; multi-hop retrieval answers complex "how does X relate to Y" questions that standard RAG misses.

deploy.note: Runs alongside LlamaIndex in agent service. Requires Qdrant (vector) + PostgreSQL (graph storage) + MinIO (source docs).

LightRAG.notes: LightRAG is additive to LlamaIndex: for class 1-4 queries, LlamaIndex suffices. For class-5 (complex multi-document reasoning over ARMES SOPs), LightRAG is invoked. The agent decides which retriever to use based on query classification.

sample.code:
# Multi-hop query over ARMES SOPs
curl -X POST http://lightrag:8020/query   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"query":"What is the procedure when oven temperature exceeds 1180C?","mode":"hybrid","tenant":"kale"}'

errors.symptom: KG construction takes hours for medium corpus (~1000 docs)
errors.action: Entity extraction is LLM-bound. Use Sonnet 4.6 not Opus for KG build (4x faster, sufficient quality). Batch size 16 optimal for parallelism.

errors.symptom: Multi-hop queries return only single-hop results
errors.action: Mode set to `local` instead of `hybrid`. Verify request body has `"mode":"hybrid"`. Local is shallow, global is broad, hybrid combines.

Graphiti + FalkorDB.desc: Temporal knowledge graph enabling class-6 causal/diagnostic queries: "Why did OEE drop on line 3 yesterday?" Graphiti processes CDC events from Redpanda and builds a time-aware property graph in FalkorDB. Distinct from LightRAG (which is for doc retrieval, not operational causality).

deploy.install: pip install graphiti-core; docker pull falkordb/falkordb
deploy.note: FalkorDB port 6379 (Redis-compat). Graphiti runs as a consumer service reading from Redpanda. Graph is built incrementally from CDC events.

Graphiti + FalkorDB.notes: Graphiti builds a temporal graph where facts have validity time ranges. A query "Why did OEE drop on 2026-05-01?" traverses the graph to find co-occurring events (maintenance, material change, operator shift) that correlate with the OEE drop.

sample.code:
# Why did OEE drop on line 3 between 14:00 and 16:00?
curl -X POST http://graphiti:8030/query   -d '{"question":"why did OEE drop","entity":"line-3","window":{"start":"2026-08-15T14:00","end":"2026-08-15T16:00"}}'

errors.symptom: Causal query returns no edges within time window
errors.action: CDC events not flowing — check Debezium connector status (`GET /connectors/pg-mfg/status`). Graphiti only knows what arrives via Redpanda topics.

errors.symptom: FalkorDB OOM with large graphs
errors.action: Default Redis memory limit too low. Set `maxmemory 8gb` in falkordb config. Consider time-window pruning: query only last 90 days unless explicitly historical.

Soda Core.desc: Data quality framework. Runs declarative quality checks (completeness, freshness, distribution, referential integrity) on Bronze/Silver/Gold tables in PostgreSQL and ClickHouse. Quality gate: if checks fail, dbt transformations are blocked.

deploy.note: No separate server. Runs as Airflow task. Check definitions in soda/ YAML files in Git.

Soda Core.notes: Required for Insurance (KVKK data quality), GU (IATF 16949 audit accuracy), and Astra (financial/board audit). Scan results are published to OpenMetadata and visible in Grafana dashboard.

ops.health: Not a service; runs as scheduled Airflow tasks
ops.metrics: soda_check_passed_total{check,dataset} emitted via custom callback; also POST results to OpenMetadata

sample.code:
# Run a Soda scan against the ClickHouse mfg warehouse
soda scan -d clickhouse   -c configuration.yml   checks/oee_quality.yml

errors.symptom: Soda scan passes but data is bad
errors.action: Checks too lenient. Audit `checks/*.yml` — `freshness < 1d` is common but for OEE you need `< 1h`. Tighten thresholds per dataset.

errors.symptom: OpenMetadata not showing scan results
errors.action: Webhook config missing. Verify `soda_publish_to_openmetadata: true` in profile.yml and check the integration token. Test with `soda scan --verbose`.

dbt Core.desc: SQL-based data transformation orchestration. Bronze (raw ingested data) → Silver (cleaned, typed, deduplicated) → Gold (business-ready aggregates). Models run in PostgreSQL and ClickHouse. Full lineage tracked in OpenMetadata.

deploy.note: No separate server. Runs as Airflow KubernetesPodOperator. dbt profiles.yml stores connection credentials from Vault.

dbt Core.notes: CWF v2 adds full medallion (F2, +400h): all ARMES and operational data sources flow through Bronze→Silver→Gold via Soda quality gates before Graphiti or agent queries.

ops.health: Not a service; runs as scheduled Airflow tasks
ops.log: {dag="dbt_silver_gold"} (also dbt artifacts in MinIO: manifest.json, run_results.json)

sample.code:
# Run gold-tier OEE model
dbt run --project-dir /app/dbt   --select gold_oee   --vars '{"tenant":"kale","period":"2026-06"}'

errors.symptom: Models fail with "duplicate column" on incremental run
errors.action: Schema drift — source added a column. dbt incremental needs `on_schema_change: append_new_columns` or `sync_all_columns`. Set in model config.

errors.symptom: Gold model has stale data despite Silver being fresh
errors.action: dbt DAG ordering issue — Gold dependency on Silver not declared via `ref()`. Use `{{ ref("silver_oee") }}` not raw table names. Check `target/manifest.json` for the dependency graph.

OpenMetadata.desc: Unified data catalog and lineage tracking. Automatically ingests metadata from PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, dbt, Soda, Airflow, and MinIO. Provides a searchable catalog of all data assets with their owners, quality scores, and end-to-end lineage.

deploy.note: Multi-container deployment. Port 8585 (UI). Requires PostgreSQL + ElasticSearch.

OpenMetadata.notes: The OpenMetadata UI is the governance dashboard for data engineers and compliance officers. Policy: every Gold table must have an owner, description, and pass Soda checks before being query-accessible by agents.

sample.code:
# Search the catalog
curl "http://openmetadata:8585/api/v1/search/query?q=oee&index=table_search_index"   -H "Authorization: Bearer $OM_TOKEN"

errors.symptom: Ingestion pipeline fails with "connection timeout"
errors.action: OpenMetadata `ingestion-bot` user lacks DB permissions. Grant `pg_read_all_data` to the user, OR specify subset of schemas in pipeline config to avoid permission errors on system tables.

errors.symptom: Search returns nothing for known tables
errors.action: Elasticsearch index out of sync. Run reindex: `POST /api/v1/search/reindex` with `{recreateIndex: true}`. Then re-trigger ingestion to populate.

Audit / SPC PDF.desc: One-click compliance PDF generation. Queries the PostgreSQL audit log, formats data into IATF 16949 / AS9100 SPC report templates (HTML + CSS), renders to PDF via WeasyPrint, and stores in MinIO. Returns download link.

deploy.note: WeasyPrint requires GTK/Cairo libs in Docker: use python:3.12-slim + apt-get install libpango-1.0 libcairo2

Audit / SPC PDF.notes: Turkish character rendering requires explicit font embedding in WeasyPrint (use Noto Sans for TR). PDF metadata includes: tenant_id, generated_at, period, approval_status. Used by Galip Usta v1 for IATF audits and Insurance for Takip audit trail.

errors.symptom: PDF generation succeeds but PDF is blank
errors.action: WeasyPrint fonts not loaded. Mount font files at `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/` in the container. Most common: Inter, Noto Sans Turkish. Verify with `fc-list | grep Turkish`.

errors.symptom: URL returned but file does not exist in MinIO
errors.action: MinIO write succeeded but bucket policy denies external read. Check bucket policy for `s3:GetObject` on `audit-pdfs/*`. Pre-signed URL bypasses this only if MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL is set.

LLM enrichment.desc: Airflow DAGs that use LiteLLM to automatically enrich data catalog entries with AI-generated descriptions, tag suggestions, and quality annotations. Reduces manual metadata effort for enterprise-scale Astra data assets.

deploy.note: Runs as scheduled Airflow DAG, not a separate service.

LLM enrichment.notes: LLM enrichment runs AFTER Soda quality checks pass. Only Gold-zone tables are enriched. Enrichment results are written to OpenMetadata via REST API.

sample.code:
# Enrich a batch of catalog rows with descriptions / tags
curl -X POST http://llm-enrich:8000/enrich   -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT"   -d '{"table":"oee_dimensions","rows":[{"id":1,"sku":"K-001"}]}'

errors.symptom: Enrichment job runs but output column is null
errors.action: LLM returned malformed JSON — enrichment expects strict schema. Check Guardrails validation logs. Add a "fallback to null" policy for production tolerance, not a hard fail.

errors.symptom: Cost exceeds budget for large batches
errors.action: Batch size too aggressive. Switch model to Haiku 4.5 for bulk enrichment, Sonnet only for high-stakes columns. Track via `enrich_cost_usd_total{table}` metric.

PostgreSQL.desc: Platform default database. Handles ALL transactional data, LangGraph state checkpoints, Keycloak users, MLflow experiments, Langfuse traces, Temporal workflows, dbt targets, Airflow metadata, and Audit logs. Native RLS for multi-tenant data isolation.

deploy.note: K8s: use Zalando postgres-operator for HA. Enable WAL (required for Debezium). Enable pgvector extension. CWF v2 adds HA (F1, +400h).

PostgreSQL.notes: CRITICAL: wal_level=logical must be set before first data ingestion if CDC is planned (CWF v2). Changing it later requires a restart. Enable pgvector immediately: CREATE EXTENSION vector; RLS policies are provisioned by Tenant Provisioning service per schema.

sample.code:
psql -h postgres -U app -d ardictech -c "SELECT count(*) FROM tenants;"
# Tenant-scoped queries use SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = '...'; for RLS enforcement.

errors.symptom: Connection pool exhausted ("too many clients")
errors.action: Application pools too large for PG `max_connections`. Sum all `pool_size * replicas` — must be < max_connections. Use pgBouncer in transaction mode for >100 concurrent.

errors.symptom: Slow queries on tenant-scoped tables
errors.action: Missing index on `tenant_id`. Run `EXPLAIN` — if Seq Scan, add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON {table}(tenant_id, ...)`. RLS without index forces sequential scan.

Redis.desc: In-memory key-value store. Serves three roles: (1) API response caching in FastAPI, (2) session state for Channel Gateway (active conversation context, TTL-based), (3) Celery broker if background task queue needed.

deploy.note: Enable AOF persistence for crash safety. Sentinel mode for HA. Port 6379.

Redis.notes: Redis data is non-critical (cache/sessions). All important state is in PostgreSQL. Redis failure degrades performance (cache misses) but does not lose data. Recovery: restart Redis, PostgreSQL is source of truth.

ops.trace: Client SDK emits redis.{cmd} (set, get, hgetall, ...)

sample.code:
redis-cli -h redis SET session:abc123 '{"user":"op-1"}' EX 14400
redis-cli -h redis GET session:abc123
# DB 0 = sessions; DB 1 = LangGraph hot state; DB 2 = rate-limit windows

errors.symptom: Sessions disappear before TTL expires
errors.action: Memory pressure causing eviction. Default `maxmemory-policy` is `noeviction` (rejects writes) or `allkeys-lru` (silent loss). Check INFO memory; raise maxmemory or shard.

errors.symptom: Rate limit returns "too many requests" for valid users
errors.action: Clock skew between pods skews sliding window. All apps must use Redis time (`TIME` command) not local time. Audit the rate limiter code.

MinIO.desc: Sovereign S3-compatible object storage. Stores: ML model artifacts (MLflow), document chunks for RAG (LlamaIndex), audit PDF outputs, Airflow XCom artifacts, and uploaded files (Web Asistan). Runs inside the sovereign cloud — no data leaves.

deploy.note: Port 9000 (S3 API), 9001 (Console UI). Use MinIO tenant operator for production. Enable bucket versioning for audit PDFs.

MinIO.notes: Bucket naming convention: {tenant_id}-{purpose} (e.g. acme-rag-docs, acme-audit-pdfs). Server-side encryption at rest with KMS key from Vault. Versioning enabled on audit-pdfs bucket for compliance.

ops.trace: mc admin trace minio | grep tenant_id  (or audit-log webhook to Loki)

sample.code:
# Upload a quarterly audit PDF and produce a 24h pre-signed URL
mc cp localfile.pdf minio/audit-pdfs/kale/2026-q2.pdf
mc share download --expire 24h minio/audit-pdfs/kale/2026-q2.pdf

errors.symptom: Pre-signed URL works for some users, 403 for others
errors.action: URL signed against MinIO internal hostname (`minio:9000`) but accessed via external URL. Set `MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL` and re-issue URLs with correct host.

errors.symptom: Tenant uploads visible across tenants
errors.action: Bucket policy missing tenant-prefix isolation. Use a single bucket per purpose (`audit-pdfs`, `catalog-files`) with `{tenant}/` prefix and policy scoped to that prefix only.

Qdrant.desc: Dedicated vector database for semantic similarity search. Stores embedding vectors for all RAG collections. Separate from pgvector: Qdrant handles large-scale, high-dimensional vector search with filtering; pgvector handles smaller-scale co-queries with relational data.

deploy.note: Port 6333 (HTTP), 6334 (gRPC). Enable snapshots to MinIO for backup. On-disk storage recommended for >10M vectors.

config.n: Payload on disk for large collections

Qdrant.notes: Qdrant collections are named {tenant_id}_{collection_type}: e.g. acme_catalog, acme_armes_docs. This gives collection-level tenant isolation. MCP server wraps Qdrant for LangGraph tool calls.

sample.code:
# Search a tenant collection
curl -X POST http://qdrant:6333/collections/kale_catalog/points/search   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"vector":[0.1, /*...1024-dim...*/],"limit":5,"with_payload":true}'

errors.symptom: Search latency p95 spikes after collection growth
errors.action: HNSW index needs rebuild as data grows. Check `index_status` — if BUILDING, queries fall back to brute force. Pre-build off-peak: `POST /collections/{name}/index`.

errors.symptom: Tenant collection deleted in error
errors.action: Qdrant has no soft-delete. Snapshot backups must exist. Restore: `POST /collections/{name}/snapshots/recover` with the latest snapshot URL from MinIO.

TimescaleDB.desc: PostgreSQL extension for time-series data. Used for sensor telemetry when Galip Usta activates sensor mode (GU sensor mode = Final/Astra phase). IoT-Ignite pushes sensor readings; TimescaleDB handles hypertable partitioning, continuous aggregates, and compression.

deploy.install: Extends existing PostgreSQL deployment OR separate instance
deploy.note: Extension: CREATE EXTENSION timescaledb; Convert tables to hypertables. Can run on same PG cluster or separate for workload isolation.

TimescaleDB.notes: Sensor mode requires IoT-Ignite adapter (G5, +300h in Final phase). TimescaleDB continuous aggregates pre-compute OEE metrics at 5-min, 1-hour, and 1-day granularities for fast dashboard queries.

ops.metrics: postgres-exporter with TimescaleDB-specific queries enabled (timescaledb_chunks, compression_ratio)
ops.trace: Same as PostgreSQL — OpenTelemetry psycopg instrumentation

sample.code:
psql -h timescaledb -d sensors -c "
  SELECT time_bucket('5m', ts) AS t, avg(value)
  FROM sensor_readings
  WHERE device = 'line3.oven' AND ts > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  GROUP BY t ORDER BY t;"

errors.symptom: Sensor inserts slow after weeks of data
errors.action: Hypertable chunks not compressed. Enable `add_compression_policy` for chunks >1 day old. Verify via `chunk_compression_stats`. Compressed chunks are 10x faster to read.

errors.symptom: Continuous aggregate stale
errors.action: Refresh policy missing. Set `add_continuous_aggregate_policy` with `schedule_interval: 1 hour`. Check `timescaledb_information.job_stats` for run history.

ClickHouse.desc: Columnar OLAP database for manufacturing analytics. Orders-of-magnitude faster than PostgreSQL for analytical queries over millions of rows (production data, quality records, OEE trends). Airbyte ingests ARMES data; Superset queries for dashboards.

deploy.note: Port 8123 (HTTP), 9000 (native). Configure max_memory_usage per query. Requires persistent volume for data.

ClickHouse.notes: ClickHouse MCP server exposes natural-language-to-SQL for LangGraph manufacturing agents (classes 1-3). Superset connects directly via JDBC for human-readable dashboards.

ops.metrics: GET http://clickhouse:9363/metrics + table system.query_log for query-level analysis
ops.trace: system.query_log table is the trace store + OTel via JDBC client

sample.code:
# Average OEE for line 3 last 7 days
curl -X POST 'http://clickhouse:8123/?database=mfg'   --data 'SELECT toDate(ts) AS d, avg(oee) FROM gold_oee WHERE line=3 AND ts > now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY d ORDER BY d FORMAT JSON'

errors.symptom: Inserts succeed but data not visible in SELECT
errors.action: ReplacingMergeTree dedupes on background merge — not visible until merged. Force with `OPTIMIZE TABLE {name} FINAL` (expensive). For low-latency reads, use `FINAL` keyword in query.

errors.symptom: Out-of-memory during large aggregation
errors.action: `max_memory_usage` too low or query needs disk spill. Set `max_bytes_before_external_group_by=10000000000` (10GB) to spill GROUP BY to disk. Last resort: pre-aggregate with materialized view.

Iceberg.desc: Apache Iceberg open table format for the data lakehouse layer. Enables ACID transactions on analytical data, time-travel queries, schema evolution, and partition pruning. Required for Astra enterprise analytics with historical audit requirements.

deploy.note: Iceberg is a table format, not a query engine. Needs a catalog (REST catalog) and a compute engine (Spark, Trino) to read/write tables. Storage: MinIO.

Iceberg.notes: Iceberg is introduced in Final phase for enterprise data lake requirements. Bronze-Silver-Gold pipeline writes Iceberg tables for Astra financial and board reporting use cases requiring time-travel (audit point-in-time queries).

ops.metrics: Catalog-level via JMX or Prometheus exporter; storage-level via MinIO

sample.code:
from pyiceberg.catalog import load_catalog
cat = load_catalog("rest", uri="http://iceberg-catalog:8181")
table = cat.load_table("finance.transactions")
# Time-travel: read the state as of EOD 2026-06-01
df = table.scan(snapshot_id=table.snapshot_by_name("2026-06-01-eod").snapshot_id).to_pandas()

errors.symptom: Time-travel query returns no data for old snapshot
errors.action: Snapshot expired by retention policy. Default 5 days. For audit, set per-table `history.expire.min-snapshots-to-keep: 100` and `history.expire.max-snapshot-age-ms: 31536000000` (1 year).

errors.symptom: Write conflicts on concurrent appends
errors.action: Iceberg uses optimistic concurrency. Two writers can collide. Retry on conflict with exponential backoff in client code. OR partition writes to avoid overlap.

MariaDB.desc: EXTERNAL: MariaDB is the ARMES MES operational database. We do NOT manage it. We ONLY read from it. MariaDB is a legacy adapter — NOT a platform component. Access is read-only via Airbyte connector and the ARMES MCP server. ⚠ v5.1 SCOPE LOCK: MariaDB/Galera exists ONLY for ARMES data replication (read-only). Never a platform transactional store. Never Galera for any new product. The insurance instance has NO MariaDB — it has no ARMES. PostgreSQL is the sole platform default.

deploy.note: Connection credentials from Vault. Read-only MySQL user required.

MariaDB.notes: Critically: never write to MariaDB. Never alter schemas. This is a read-only integration point. The existing ARMES MCP server already handles the abstraction layer.

Airflow.desc: Workflow orchestration for all batch data pipelines. Manages: daily dbt transformation runs, Soda quality check scans, OpenMetadata ingestion, document re-indexing for RAG, and scheduled report generation. KubernetesExecutor for isolation.

deploy.note: KubernetesExecutor: each task runs in its own K8s pod. Port 8080 (UI). Requires PostgreSQL for metadata.

Airflow.notes: DAG patterns: (1) dbt_run → soda_scan → openmetadata_sync (daily pipeline), (2) rag_reindex (triggered on new doc upload), (3) audit_report (weekly, on-demand). DAGs are GitSynced — no manual upload needed.

ops.log: {service="airflow"} | json | dag="..."  (task instance logs in MinIO)

sample.code:
# Trigger a DAG via REST API
curl -X POST http://airflow:8080/api/v1/dags/rag_reindex/dagRuns   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"conf":{"tenant":"kale","collection":"catalog"}}'

errors.symptom: Scheduler runs but no tasks execute
errors.action: Worker pool full or DAG paused. Check `airflow_pool` and DAG state in UI. Common: pool size 1, all slots held by long-running task. Raise pool or split DAG.

errors.symptom: Task succeeds but downstream marked "upstream failed"
errors.action: XCom serialization issue — task returns non-JSON-serializable object. Check task logs. Convert objects to dict before returning.

File upload.desc: FastAPI endpoint that accepts manufacturer catalog files (CSV, XLS, PDF). Validates format, stores in MinIO, triggers an Airflow DAG to chunk, embed, and index into Qdrant for RAG retrieval. Progress streamed back to admin dashboard.

deploy.install: pip install python-multipart pypdf pandas openpyxl
deploy.note: Max file size configurable. Virus scanning recommended (ClamAV sidecar).

File upload.notes: File processing is async: upload returns immediately with a job_id. Admin dashboard polls /jobs/{job_id}/status. On success, Qdrant collection is updated and the RAG index is immediately queryable.

errors.symptom: Upload succeeds but RAG re-index never runs
errors.action: Airflow DAG trigger failed silently. Check `file_upload.last_triggered_dag` audit field. Re-trigger manually: `curl -X POST {airflow}/api/v1/dags/rag_reindex/dagRuns`.

errors.symptom: Large file uploads timeout
errors.action: Kong has 60s body timeout by default. Set `body_timeout: 300` on the file-upload route OR use multipart resumable uploads via tus.io protocol.

NiFi SMB crawler.desc: Apache NiFi flow that crawls Windows SMB network shares (insurance bound/submissions folders), reads new files, extracts text from PDFs, indexes document metadata into PostgreSQL, and pushes document vectors into Qdrant for fuzzy search.

deploy.note: Port 8443 (HTTPS UI). Configure flow.xml.gz via NiFi REST API or Git. SMB processor requires NiFi SMB extension.

NiFi SMB crawler.notes: NiFi polls the SMB share every 5 minutes. New files trigger extraction, embedding, and indexing. Duplicate detection: SHA256 hash stored in PostgreSQL. NiFi is Insurance-specific — not a platform-wide ingestion tool.

ops.trace: NiFi flowfile lineage via /nifi-api/provenance/lineage (per-flowfile UUID is the trace key)

sample.code:
# Trigger an on-demand processor run
curl -X PUT http://nifi:8080/nifi-api/processors/{processor_id}/run-status   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"   -d '{"state":"RUNNING","revision":{"version":1}}'

errors.symptom: Files in SMB share but not pulled
errors.action: NiFi `GetSmbFile` processor may have hit `KeepSourceFile=false` and moved them. Verify with `ListSmbFile` instead. Check NiFi UI for processor state — most failures are FAILED with auth errors.

errors.symptom: Duplicate processing of same file
errors.action: NiFi state store reset (e.g., on pod restart with ephemeral storage). Use persistent volume for `state.directory` OR shift dedup to SHA256-based logic at the FastAPI ingest layer.

Airbyte.desc: Open-source data integration platform with 300+ pre-built connectors. Primary use: sync ARMES/MariaDB operational data to ClickHouse for analytics and to PostgreSQL for operational queries. Manages incremental syncs with CDC-light (cursor-based).

deploy.note: Port 8000 (UI). K8s runner for connector pods. Requires PostgreSQL for state.

Airbyte.notes: ARMES connector: MariaDB source → ClickHouse destination. Sync frequency: 15-minute incremental. Full refresh weekly for consistency check. Airbyte state table tracks last synced cursor per stream.

errors.symptom: Sync runs but no records moved
errors.action: Source connector schema discovery returned empty. Refresh source schema in UI — common after MariaDB column adds. Check connector logs for "Discovery returned 0 streams".

errors.symptom: Destination ClickHouse rejects records
errors.action: Type mapping issue — Airbyte sends BigDecimal where ClickHouse wants Float64. Either configure type override in destination, or use a transformation step (dbt staging model).

Debezium + Redpanda.desc: Change Data Capture pipeline: Debezium monitors PostgreSQL WAL (write-ahead log) and publishes every row-level change event (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) to Redpanda (Kafka-compatible) topics. Graphiti consumes these events to build the temporal knowledge graph.

deploy.note: Debezium: port 8083 (Kafka Connect REST). Redpanda: port 9092 (Kafka API). Both require persistent volumes.

Debezium + Redpanda.notes: PostgreSQL must have wal_level=logical (set at Core install, A2). Replication slot accumulates WAL if consumer is down — monitor slot lag to prevent disk fill. Redpanda topics: ardictech.public.{table_name}. Graphiti subscribes to manufacturing-related tables.

ops.health: Debezium: GET http://debezium:8083/connectors/{name}/status   ·   Redpanda: rpk cluster health
ops.metrics: Debezium JMX → Prometheus (debezium_replication_lag) · Redpanda GET http://redpanda:9644/metrics
ops.trace: CDC events carry LSN + ts; trace as cdc.{table}.{lsn}

sample.code:
# Register a new Debezium Postgres source connector
curl -X POST http://debezium:8083/connectors   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"name":"pg-mfg","config":{"connector.class":"io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector","database.hostname":"postgres","database.dbname":"mfg","plugin.name":"pgoutput","slot.name":"debezium_mfg","topic.prefix":"mfg"}}'

errors.symptom: Replication lag growing
errors.action: Consumer (Graphiti) slow or stopped. Check `kafka_consumer_lag` metric per topic. Common: Graphiti pod restart loop. Restart consumer with `--from-beginning` for full catch-up if acceptable.

errors.symptom: WAL bloat on Postgres source
errors.action: Replication slot `debezium_mfg` inactive. If Debezium pod crashed without graceful shutdown, slot accumulates WAL. Drop and recreate: `SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot("debezium_mfg")` then restart connector.

IoT-Ignite.desc: EXTERNAL platform (owned by partner). Manages all edge sensors, gateways, and device provisioning for Galip Usta sensor mode. WE DO NOT BUILD ANY IoT/edge infrastructure. We ONLY build the adapter: an HTTP REST endpoint that accepts IoT-Ignite telemetry pushes and writes to TimescaleDB.

deploy.image: IoT-Ignite manages edge — no containers by us
deploy.note: IoT-Ignite pushes data to our endpoint. We configure the push target in the IoT-Ignite portal.

IoT-Ignite.notes: GU v1 has NO sensors. Sensor mode comes in Final/Astra phase (G5, +300h). When active: IoT-Ignite pushes telemetry every 30s → adapter validates and writes to TimescaleDB → LangGraph agents query for predictive maintenance.

ARMES MES.desc: EXTERNAL: Core manufacturing execution system. IMPORTANT: The ARMES MCP server is ALREADY DEVELOPED (confirmed fact). This eliminates the principal CWF integration risk. We connect via the existing MCP adapter — no need to build a new integration layer.

deploy.note: ARMES MCP exposes manufacturing data (work orders, quality records, OEE, equipment status) as LangGraph tool calls.

ARMES MES.notes: The ARMES MCP being pre-built saves 240h (E1 reduced 400h→160h). LangGraph calls ARMES data via MCP tool call exactly like calling any other tool. No direct SQL to MariaDB from agent code.

sample.code:
# Call the ARMES MCP tool via JSON-RPC (LangGraph does this internally)
curl -X POST http://armes-mcp:3001/jsonrpc   -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCP_TOKEN"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_work_orders","arguments":{"line":"3","date":"2026-06-03"}},"id":1}'

errors.symptom: MCP tool calls return "tool not found"
errors.action: MCP server not advertising the tool. Verify `armes-mcp` tool list: `curl http://armes-mcp:3001/jsonrpc -d '{"method":"tools/list"}'`. Common: tool added in code but service not restarted.

errors.symptom: ARMES queries slow (>5s)
errors.action: MariaDB connection pool starved or MES system overloaded. Check `mes_query_latency_ms` p95. Move heavy historical queries to ClickHouse mirror via Airbyte sync.

Exchange / Graph.desc: EXTERNAL: Microsoft Exchange mailbox accessed via Microsoft Graph API. Used for Insurance: incoming email (new facultative submissions) triggers the triage workflow. Outgoing replies sent via Graph. NOT an internal platform — pure external integration.

deploy.install: Microsoft Graph SDK: pip install msgraph-sdk
deploy.note: App registration in Azure AD with Mail.Read + Mail.Send delegated/application permissions.

ARU / KARU.desc: EXTERNAL: Türk Reasürans internal lookup systems (Aktif Risk Ünitleri / Kabul Reddedilen Üniteleri). Used for insurance triage: check if a facultative offer has been seen before. ⚠️ BIGGEST RISK: Unknown if API is available (80h) or requires UI scraping (320h).

deploy.install: Week-1 spike required to determine integration method
deploy.note: If REST API: integrate via requests. If web UI only: Playwright-based scraping (fragile, maintenance burden).

ARU / KARU.notes: ⚠️ ARU/KARU is the single biggest risk to the insurance M3 commercial gate (Variant B). Week-1 discovery spike is MANDATORY if Variant B is chosen. If UI-scrape: add Playwright + extra 240h. If API: standard REST integration at 80h.

SMB shares.desc: EXTERNAL: Windows network file shares at Türk Re. Contains historical insurance submissions (bound folder) and current incoming submissions. NiFi SMB Crawler reads these folders. Two folders: /Submissions (incoming) and /Bound (accepted historical).

deploy.install: NiFi SMB Processor accesses via credentials

SAP.desc: EXTERNAL: SAP enterprise systems for Astra financial and inventory use cases. S/4HANA via OData services. BW/BPC via MDX queries. Exposed to LangGraph via SAP MCP server (G2, +720h in Final phase).

deploy.install: SAP MCP: build in Final phase (G2)
deploy.note: SAP OData: /sap/opu/odata/SAP/. RFC BAPI via pyrfc or sapjco3.

sample.code:
# Fetch stock levels via SAP MCP
curl -X POST http://sap-mcp:3002/jsonrpc   -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCP_TOKEN"   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_stock","arguments":{"plant":"K001","material":"M-1234"}},"id":1}'

errors.symptom: RFC connection drops mid-query
errors.action: SAP gateway timeout. Set `WDISP/HTTP/MAX_REQUEST_LENGTH` higher on SAP side. Also configure connection pooling in MCP server — do not open RFC per request.

errors.symptom: Auth fails after 24h of working fine
errors.action: SAP service user password expired. Use a service user with "Password Never Expires" or rotate via Vault on schedule. Check SAP login audit (SM21) for the failure reason.

SharePoint.desc: EXTERNAL: SharePoint document libraries accessed via Microsoft Graph API. Used in Astra for document-based knowledge retrieval (SOPs, policies, board documents). SharePoint MCP server built in Final phase.

deploy.install: SharePoint MCP: build in Final phase (G2)

sample.code:
# Search documents on an enterprise SharePoint site
curl -X POST http://sharepoint-mcp:3003/jsonrpc   -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCP_TOKEN"   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"search_documents","arguments":{"site":"engineering","query":"IATF audit 2026"}},"id":1}'

errors.symptom: Search returns no results despite documents existing
errors.action: Graph API search requires indexing. Check `enable-search` site config. Also: service principal needs `Sites.Read.All` application permission, not just `Sites.Read.Selected`.

errors.symptom: Document download returns 401
errors.action: Token expired between search and download. MCP server must refresh OAuth token if older than 50min. Implement token cache with refresh — do not hold token in memory across requests.

Salesforce.desc: EXTERNAL: Salesforce CRM via REST API and SOQL queries. Used in Astra for customer/contract data in UC4 Multi-channel. Salesforce MCP server built in Final phase.

deploy.install: Salesforce MCP: build in Final phase (G2)

sample.code:
# Query opportunities via Salesforce MCP
curl -X POST http://salesforce-mcp:3004/jsonrpc   -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCP_TOKEN"   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"query_opportunities","arguments":{"soql":"SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity WHERE StageName="Closed Won" AND CloseDate=THIS_QUARTER"}},"id":1}'

errors.symptom: SOQL returns "INVALID_FIELD" for custom field
errors.action: Custom field API name (`Foo__c`) used but field renamed in SF. Re-fetch object metadata: `GET /services/data/v59.0/sobjects/Opportunity/describe`. Update field references.

errors.symptom: Bulk query hits governor limit
errors.action: SOQL row limit (50k for sync, 2k chunks for async). Switch to Bulk API 2.0 for >50k. Or paginate via `LIMIT` + `OFFSET` (max OFFSET 2000).

Kubernetes.desc: Container orchestration platform. All platform components run as K8s Deployments, StatefulSets, or Jobs. Tenant isolation via namespaces + NetworkPolicies. HPA for auto-scaling. Sovereign deployment on Netaş/OSB Cloud.

deploy.install: K8s cluster provisioned by cloud provider
deploy.note: Minimum: 3 control plane nodes + 4 worker nodes (2 GPU nodes for vLLM). NetworkPolicy enabled. StorageClass for persistent volumes.

Kubernetes.notes: Key K8s patterns: (1) Each tenant in its own namespace with ResourceQuota, (2) NetworkPolicy: pods can only reach services in their namespace + platform-system, (3) PodDisruptionBudgets on stateful services, (4) GPU nodes tainted, only vLLM tolerates.

ArgoCD.desc: GitOps continuous deployment. Platform configuration (Helm values, Kustomize overlays) lives in Git. ArgoCD watches the repo and automatically syncs K8s state to match Git. Every deployment is traceable, reversible, and auditable.

deploy.note: Port 443 (HTTPS UI). Configure app-of-apps pattern. Webhook from Git for instant sync.

ArgoCD.notes: App-of-apps pattern: one ArgoCD Application per platform component. Parent "platform" app manages all children. Rollback: git revert + ArgoCD auto-syncs within 3 minutes.

OpenTofu.desc: Declarative Infrastructure-as-Code for the layer BELOW Kubernetes: provisions the sovereign K8s cluster, GPU node pools (for vLLM), object-storage backing for MinIO, network/VPC, DNS, and StorageClasses on Netaş/OSB. MPL-2.0 Linux Foundation fork of Terraform — chosen over Terraform to avoid the BUSL license question on a sovereign deployment. The entire cluster is rebuildable from Git.

deploy.image: ghcr.io/opentofu/opentofu:latest (CI runner) — not a cluster workload
deploy.install: tofu init && tofu plan && tofu apply
deploy.note: Runs from the CI pipeline, not inside the cluster. State stored in MinIO S3 backend with state locking. Modules: cluster, node-pools, gpu-pool, dns, object-store.

config.n: Remote state on sovereign object storage

OpenTofu.notes: CRITICAL GAP CLOSED: without IaC, the cluster exists only as long as nobody touches it and cannot be rebuilt or replicated for a second sovereign tenant. OpenTofu makes A1 reproducible. Recommendation over Pulumi (avoids adding a new language surface) and Crossplane (avoids running a second control plane at single-cluster scale).

CI pipeline.desc: Continuous Integration: the build half of the pipeline that ArgoCD assumes already exists. On every commit: lints, runs tests, builds container images, scans for vulnerabilities (Trivy), pushes to the sovereign registry, and bumps the image tag in the GitOps repo — which triggers ArgoCD to deploy. Self-hosted runner inside the sovereign cluster so build artifacts never leave Turkish jurisdiction.

deploy.install: helm install gitlab-runner gitlab/gitlab-runner OR ARC for GitHub
deploy.note: Runner deployed as K8s pods with ephemeral build executors. Registry credentials from Vault. Avoid Jenkins — maintenance burden too high for a 10-FTE team.

CI pipeline.notes: CRITICAL GAP CLOSED: GitOps is deployment-only — it assumes images exist in a registry and that the manifest was updated. CI is the missing build-test-push half. The flow is: commit → CI builds + tests + scans + pushes image → CI bumps tag in GitOps repo → ArgoCD syncs. Keeps everything inside the sovereign boundary. New task A4.5.

Container registry.desc: Self-hosted, sovereign container image registry. Stores all custom-built platform images (FastAPI, LangGraph, Channel Gateway, Memori, Audit PDF, MCP servers) plus cached upstream images. Harbor adds vulnerability scanning, image signing (Cosign), and replication. Required because a sovereign deployment cannot depend on a public registry as a runtime dependency.

deploy.note: Backed by MinIO for image layers and PostgreSQL for metadata. Port 443. Robot accounts for CI push and K8s pull, credentials in Vault.

config.n: Image layer storage on sovereign object store
Sign images, K8s verifies on pull

Container registry.notes: Closes the loop between CI and ArgoCD: CI pushes here, K8s pulls from here. Image signing (Cosign) + admission policy means only signed images run in production. Harbor reuses MinIO and PostgreSQL — no new datastore introduced.

Grafana + Prometheus.desc: Metrics collection (Prometheus) and visualization (Grafana). Platform dashboards: K8s cluster health, service latencies, LLM inference throughput, token costs, data quality scores, tenant usage, and RAG hit rates.

deploy.note: Includes Prometheus, Grafana, AlertManager, and node exporter. Port 3000 (Grafana).

Grafana + Prometheus.notes: Key dashboards: (1) Platform Overview: SLA, error rates, active sessions; (2) LLM Dashboard: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, cost per tenant; (3) Data Quality: Soda check pass rates; (4) RAG Performance: retrieval latency, relevance scores.

Loki + OTel.desc: Loki (log aggregation) + OpenTelemetry Collector (distributed tracing). Every service ships logs to Loki via FluentBit sidecar. OTel Collector receives OTLP traces from LangGraph, FastAPI, and other services, then forwards to Langfuse (AI traces) and Grafana (system traces).

deploy.note: OTel Collector: deploy as DaemonSet. Loki: requires object storage (MinIO).

Loki + OTel.notes: OTel trace propagation: every HTTP request into the platform carries a trace_id header. LangGraph, FastAPI, and other services propagate this header. End-to-end traces are visible from user message to LLM response in both Langfuse (AI focus) and Grafana (infra focus).

Vault.desc: Centralized secrets management. ALL credentials (DB passwords, API keys, signing keys, TLS certs) are stored in Vault, never in K8s Secrets directly. K8s CSI driver injects secrets as environment variables into pods at startup.

deploy.note: HA mode: Raft storage. Port 8200. Enable K8s Auth backend. Enable KV-v2 secrets engine.

Vault.notes: K8s auth: pods authenticate to Vault using their K8s ServiceAccount JWT. Vault validates with K8s API and issues a short-lived token. Secrets are dynamically injected via Vault Agent Sidecar or CSI driver. No static credentials in Git or K8s Secrets.

Cert mgr + Wireguard.desc: cert-manager automates TLS certificate issuance and renewal (Let's Encrypt or internal CA via Vault PKI). Wireguard provides VPN tunnels for sovereign inter-datacenter links and for connecting external systems (ARMES, SMB shares, ARU/KARU) securely.

deploy.note: cert-manager port: no external port. Wireguard port: 51820 UDP.

Cert mgr + Wireguard.notes: All inter-service communication uses mTLS. cert-manager auto-renews before expiry. Wireguard tunnels: ARMES database access, Türk Re SMB share access, ARU/KARU system access — all over VPN, never over public internet.

Evidently AI.desc: ML model monitoring. Detects drift in LLM output quality (embedding drift, response length distribution, RAGAS score degradation) and data distribution shifts. Alerts Grafana when drift exceeds thresholds.

deploy.image: Custom Airflow DAGs using evidently library
deploy.note: Runs as scheduled Airflow DAG. Results pushed to Grafana via Prometheus remote_write.

Evidently AI.notes: Drift detection is CRITICAL before CWF v2 goes live with full medallion data. Any significant drift triggers a LangGraph prompt review cycle and MLflow evaluation run.
